latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 6394Q
London BTC Company Limited
14 August 2026
LONDON BTC COMPANY LIMITED
US Critical Mineral Antimony Targeted for Nevada Exploration
London, New York, 14 August 2026 - London BTC Company Limited
("Company") (BTC: LSE, VINZF: OTCQB), the London Stock Exchange main market-listed company is pleased to announce that high-grade
Antimony ("Sb")
has been recorded only 120 metres south of the Company's
Black Star Gold-Silver Project
(the "Project" or "Black Star") in Nevada, USA and the Company is excited and optimistic that Antimony may also have the potential to be present on its Black Star mineral claims.
On 15 July 2026, the Company announced a gold discovery in Nevada with surface sampling reporting grades up to
16.23 g/t (0.52 oz/t Au) and 50.5 g/t silver (1.62 oz/t Ag)
.
It has now been determined that the gold and silver mineralisation at Black Star sits within the same trending mineralised corridor as reported Antimony mineralisation immediately to the south of the Company's mineral claims.
Detailed research by the Company's geological team has identified key and important historical data highlighting the area's potential for hosting high-grade of Antimony discoveries.
Antimony is designated as a critical mineral in the United States
, reflecting its importance to U.S. economic and national security and the vulnerability of its supply chain. Antimony also has important defense applications, including its use in ammunition and other military systems.
David Lenigas, Chairman of the Company, stated,
"Since its initial due diligence and ground staking, Black Star has consistently provided high-quality results. We staked this ground for its potential of high-grade gold, and the work our technical consultant has done since has now identified a critical mineral as a potential by-product of the mineralisation. A trend holding over 1% Antimony and up to 16.23 grams per tonne gold is exactly the type of asset we want in our portfolio. The United States is import-dependent for Antimony and is actively funding domestic supply, so a gold-silver project like Black Star, which may also carry an Antimony credit, is a materially more attractive proposition than either metal on its own."
Key Points
• A review of USGS and NBMG archive data has identified historical data proximal to the intrusion-related Black Star system grading
greater than 1% Antimony (>10,000 ppm Sb)
. The result exceeded the upper limit of the analytical method used, and the true Antimony grade is unknown (USGS, MRDS, 1985).
• Antimony is designated a
critical
and
strategic
mineral
by the United States Government. The USGS reports that the United States remain substantially import-reliant for Antimony, and that Antimony is one of the minerals subject to Chinese export restrictions on shipments to the United States (USGS, 2025).
• The US government has committed to a
$12 billion stockpile
to establish an inventory from critical and strategic mineral projects, including $10 billion in funding from the US Export-Import Bank (EXIM) and a further $2 billion in private funding (Reuters, 2026).
• Gold projects carrying an Antimony credit are attracting significant strategic capital in the United States. In May 2026 EXIM approved a
US$2.9 billion
senior secured loan for Perpetua Resources' Stibnite Gold Project in Idaho, a gold-Antimony development (Perpetua Resources, 2026).
•
Recent engagement with
Dahrouge Geological Consulting
allows for immediate access to experienced field personnel for further sampling, geological mapping and technical assessment.
• The Black Star project consists of
36 mineral claims over 744 acres (3 km2)
in Pershing County, Nevada. Approximately 60 miles (96 km) from the Company's Huntington-Whitman Project and 73 miles (117 km) from its Amonett-Frank Project.
• The Antimony-bearing sample lies approximately
120 m south
of the Black Star claims and within the same structural corridor that returned
16.23 g/t Au and 50.5 g/t Ag
from the Company's 2026 due diligence rock chip programme conducted by Schiehallion Consulting.
• Economic Sb is a recognised part of hydrothermal Au-Ag systems in the USA. The value and potential of these projects are demonstrated by the Meadow Creek region of Idaho, which represents a domestic development for the economic extraction of Gold and Antimony.
• The historical sample also returned
2% copper
,
700 ppm silver
, 1,000 ppm arsenic, 1,000 ppm bismuth and 700 ppm lead. This is an association characteristic of Cu-Sb-Ag sulphosalt mineralisation of the tetrahedrite group.
• This historical sample sits within mineralisation which is interpreted to occupy within the same structural trend and host rock as the sampled Black Star mineralisation. While no modern Antimony assays exist for Black Star, new Au-Sb assays will be a priority for the asset.
• Antimony was
not included in the analytical suite
used for the Company's 2026 rock chip programme, which was assayed for gold and silver only. Antimony will be included as standard in all future analytical suites at Black Star.
• Field Teams will be mobilised in late August, and new Gold-Antimony sampling around Black Star is a priority for these teams.
CEO Commentary
Hewie Rattray, CEO of the Company, stated:
"Black Star is rapidly developing into one of the most exciting assets in our Nevada portfolio. We originally secured the project for its high-grade gold potential, with initial sampling returning up to 16.23 g/t gold, but the identification of historical antimony mineralisation grading in excess of 1% just 120 metres from our claims adds a potentially significant new dimension to the project. At a time when the United States is placing strategic importance on securing domestic supplies of critical minerals, we believe Black Star is well positioned. Our upcoming field programme will now target this gold-silver-antimony system aggressively, and we are very excited about what the next phase of exploration could reveal."
Antimony at Black Star
The Project comprises of 36 unpatented mineral claims over 744 acres (3 km²) (Figure 1). The staked ground focuses on the historically targeted geological contact between metavolcanics and granodiorite. The contact is targeted by shafts, adits and prospect pits. A review of government databases, technical literature and historical company reports identified limited follow-up exploration since the 1980s (USGS, MRDS Records).
Historical sampling at Black Star was undertaken by the Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology in June 1985 as part of a regional mineral inventory of the Sonoma-Gerlach Resource Area (USGS, MRDS, 1985) and is captured in the USGS Mineral Resource Data System.
Three rock samples were collected across the historical workings, sample IDs: 2928, 2929, and 2930. These samples were analysed by semi-quantitative emission spectrography, with gold determined by atomic absorption.

MSALABS dried, crushed and pulverised the samples, which were then separated into 500g jars. Utilising Chrysos Corporation's PhotonAssay™ method, results were obtained within days of submission. PhotonAssay™ holds a lower detection limit of 0.015 ppm. Samples were routinely submitted for Fire Assay as part of follow-up QA/QC to confirm the validity of high-grade results. Fire Assay results were comparable to PhotonAssay™ results.
Further information relating to this sampling programme can be found in the Company's RNS dated 15th July 2026 titled 'Gold Discovery in Nevada, USA'.
Further information relating to QAQC verification of samples can be found in the Company's RNS dated 5th August 2026 titled 'Gold Assays Return up to 143.1 g/t in Nevada USA'.
Antimony and United States Critical Minerals Policy
Antimony is a designated critical and strategic mineral by the United States Government based on its importance to national defence and industry. Antimony is used in a range of defence applications, including ammunition, night vision equipment and infrared optics (CSIS, 2024). Global mine supply of Antimony is dominated by China, which has enacted export restrictions on the commodity. Additionally, there have been intermittent restrictions on the use of Chinese Antimony for end use in US military and defence weapon systems, exposing a gap in the US defence sector (CSIS, 2024). Following these developments, the US has publicly announced its support for domestic critical mineral supply chains and has backed this with significant investment through federal and national programmes.
In 2025, the United States Geological Survey (USGS) reported that the United States remained reliant on imports from China for 14 of 33 critical minerals for which it was import-dependent, with Antimony amongst the commodities subject to Chinese export restrictions to the US. To combat dependence on foreign nations, the US government has committed to a $12 billion stockpile of critical and strategic minerals through the use of the US EXIM Bank and private funding (Reuters, 2026).
Antimony prices responded accordingly, with international assessments rising to a peak of US$59,750 per tonne in July 2025 (Fastmarkets, 2026). China, Tajikistan, Russia, Bolivia and Myanmar dominate primary Antimony production; as a result, geopolitics is a key driver of the Antimony market, though this is primarily fuelled by US-China trade tensions (Fastmarkets, 2026).
The response in domestic exploration and recycling has been significant, though the building of alternative supply chains takes time. The US EXIM Bank has been a key catalyst in the development of domestic Antimony infrastructure, approving a US$2.9 billion senior secured long-term loan to Perpetua Resources Corp. (NASDAQ: PPTA) for the Stibnite Gold Project in Idaho, a gold project with a significant Antimony component, under the Make More in America Initiative (Perpetua Resources, 2026). The loan becomes available pending completion of definitive conditions expected in the second half of 2026.
Antimony is a critical and strategic mineral in the US, with global geopolitical tensions fuelling a favourable market outlook (Fastmarkets, 2026). For the Company to be exploring an Au-Ag-Sb system in Nevada, consistently ranked among the world's most attractive mining jurisdictions (Fraser Institute, 2025), positions the Company and the Black Star project within a supply chain that both federal policy and private capital are actively building. However, gold and silver will remain the primary focus of future exploration developments.
Strategic Significance for the Company
The Black Star area was staked based on its Au-Ag potential. The Project fulfilled multiple geological criteria in the targeting stage and presented a prospective target for due diligence sampling and subsequent staking. The Black Star project provided significant upside with demonstrated high-grade Au-Ag mineralisation, a large untested footprint with immediate targets, and system-scale potential. The presence of Antimony mineralisation was previously unweighted in the assessment of project value; newfound research opens potential for Antimony credits.
Black Star remains a gold-silver exploration project. The significance of the Antimony data is that it introduces the possibility of a critical mineral alongside precious metals, in a jurisdiction where domestic critical mineral supply receives direct and substantial government support. Should Antimony mineralisation be confirmed within the Black Star project, it would open the Project to potential development and funding pathways available, including United States critical minerals programmes.
The recovery of Antimony would be de-risked if recovered as a by-product of a gold operation. Antimony would represent a credit rather than the sole basis for development, with reliance on gold to cover operational costs.
The Antimony result of greater than 10,000 ppm Sb from sample 2930 is significant and materially affects exploration strategy at the Black Star project. Further sampling of mineralisation at Black Star, with the inclusion of Antimony in the assay suite, is now a high priority to determine overall Antimony grade and consistency within Au-Ag mineralisation.
Geological Interpretation
The mineralisation at the Black Star project is developed across a major contact between metavolcanic rocks to the east and granodiorite to the west, with the majority of historical workings following north-northwest trending quartz veins hosted within the granodiorite (USGS, MRDS). The Company has previously reported the presence of black tourmaline adjacent to contact zones, together with an intrusion-related geochemical signature, as supporting a proximal fertile intrusion at depth.
Antimony is found within intrusion-related systems, though it is rarely formed in economic concentrations. The most probable interpretation for the presence of Antimony would be the hydrothermal enrichment and concentration of the element alongside Au-Ag mineralisation. However, the source, consistency and extent of Antimony are currently unknown, so this interpretation should be treated as conceptual.
Further geological interpretation at this stage requires confirmation of local Antimony grade and an understanding of geological and geochemical setting. Sampling of Au-Ag-Sb mineralisation will be a priority for the Company. This field programme will be immediately followed by updated assay information, further information on the geological setting and insight into the economic relevance of mineralisation.
Figure 2: Black Star Project regional setting, Pershing County, Northern Nevada
Forward Work Programme
• If recoverable, multi-element re-assay of sample material from the Company's 2026 rock chip programme to include Antimony.
• Comprehensive rock chip sampling of the 2.5 km corridor between target zones, clustering around quartz networks and zones of alteration. All samples to be assayed for Au-Ag-Sb.
• Rock chip sampling programme extended to the South-East to target mineralisation trending from the historical Au-Ag-Sb recorded sample site onto the Company's mineral claims.
• Geological mapping to define the structural setting and economic significance of the separate components of the mineral system, focus on intrusion-hydrothermal relationships.
• Compilation of geoscientific data to assist in the understanding of the local geology, alteration and structural setting and to provide drill-ready targets.
• Progression of further gold and silver project staking in Nevada and Arizona, in line with the Company's previously announced phased strategy.

About London BTC Company Limited
The Company's primary listing is on the London Stock Exchange (United Kingdom) under the ticker "BTC.L" and it trades in the USA on the OTCQB under the ticker "VINZF". The Company is building up a strategic Bitcoin holding through acquiring Bitcoin as a treasury and currency management tool and through adding Bitcoin generated from its mining operations in North America. The Company currently operates Bitcoin miners hosted across multiple third-party facilities in Indiana, Iowa, Nebraska and Texas (USA) and Labrador (Canada). As part of its hedging strategy, the Company has begun building a portfolio of US gold assets in the Tier 1 gold jurisdiction of Nevada, to complement its core Bitcoin treasury and mining operations, thereby providing shareholders with exposure to two scarce and globally recognised stores of value.
Cautionary Statement
This announcement contains references to technical information sourced from third-party reports, public databases, technical literature and government reports, including historical analytical results collected by the Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology in 1985 and published by the United States Geological Survey. These historical results have not been verified by the Company, have not been verified by a Competent Person, are not reported in compliance with any current Mineral Resource or Ore Reserve code, and should not be relied upon as indicative of the prospectivity of the Project or of any future resource, reserve or production from the Project.
The Company emphasises that no economic study has been undertaken at Black Star, that no Mineral Resource has been estimated, and there is no certainty that the historical Antimony results described in this announcement will be reproduced by modern sampling or that a deposit of economic significance is present. This cannot be confirmed with the current information available at the project.
All the samples discussed in this release are selective in nature with a high potential for bias and should not be considered as being representative of the overall mineralised structure or zone.
While the alteration, mineralisation styles and metal associations observed to date show similarities to systems in the region and elsewhere, all such comparisons are conceptual only. There is no assurance that mineralisation encountered at Black Star will be comparable in scale, grade, mineralogy or economic characteristics to any other deposit or project referred to in this announcement. References to third-party projects, financings and government programmes are provided for market context only and do not imply that Black Star is of comparable merit or that the Company has applied for, or expects to receive, any form of government support.
Competent Person's Statement
The information in this report that relates to exploration results and technical information is based on information compiled by Fionnlagh (Finn) Hunter, Principal Geological Consultant at Schiehallion Consulting, who is a Member of the Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy (AusIMM) and has sufficient experience of relevance to the styles of mineralisation and the types of deposits under consideration, and to the activities undertaken, to qualify as a Competent Person as defined in the 2012 Edition of the Joint Ore Reserves Committee (JORC) Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves. Mr Hunter consents to the inclusion in this report of the matters based on the information in the form and context in which it appears.
The directors of London BTC Company Limited accept responsibility for this announcement.

London BTC Company Limited
05 August 2026
LONDON BTC COMPANY LIMITED
Outstanding Gold Assays Return up to 143.1 g/t in Nevada USA
New assays return 143.1 g/t Au - the highest gold grade to date across the Company's US portfolio, previous assay verification completed and additional US consultant appointed
Issue of Employee Benefits Trust Shares
London, New York, 05 August 2026 - London BTC Company Limited
("Company") (BTC: LSE, VINZF: OTCQB), the London Stock Exchange main market-listed company is pleased to announce new assay results received from its
Amonett-Frank Gold-Silver Project
(the "Project", "Amonett-Frank Project" or "Amonett-Frank") in Nevada, USA.
The Company also announces the completion of assay verification across its full US portfolio and the engagement of
Dahrouge Geological Consulting
("Dahrouge") as its US-based consultant, significantly increasing exploration capacity.
"143 grams of gold per tonne is a truly exceptional grade at Amonett-Frank," said David Lenigas, the Company's Chairman. "Just as importantly, we have now put every one of our high-grade results through fire assay verification and have validated all of our previously announced high-grade results reported from our Nevada portfolio. This gives us real confidence in the quality of the ground we have secured thus far. Additionally, we have appointed Dahrouge to scale up our operations in the United States, as we swiftly move from staking into active exploration across the portfolio."
Key Points
·
Further samples over Amonett-Frank have returned
outstanding high-grade gold
, across the Project:
o
Amonett-Frank Project, BTCRK33,
143.1 g/t Au
o
Amonett-Frank Project, BTCRK31,
12.62 g/t Au
o
Amonett-Frank Project, BTCRK32,
1.22 g/t Au
·
The peak result of
143.1 g/t Au
(4.60 oz/t Au) is the
highest gold grade returned to date
across the Company's US gold portfolio. This sample was over-limit for fire assay; the value was obtained by QA/QC gravimetric finish, which delayed routine assay turnaround.
·
The project sits
2.6 miles (4.2 km) from the Goldbanks Au resource
, with an endowment of 2.56 Moz Au and 7.47 Moz Ag (Stone, 2010) (Kinross U.S., NYSE: KGC). Amonett-Frank shares the broader region with the Barrick-Newmont Nevada Gold Mines Joint Venture (NGM), which owns and operates six significant Au mines within the region.
·
All PhotonAssay™ results across the Company's US projects were re-submitted for fire assay as part of the Company's QA/QC protocol. The fire assay results were comparable to the reported PhotonAssay™ results, confirming the validity of the reported grades.
·
Assay verification of the PhotonAssay™ allows the Company to utilise this technique for routine analysis, reducing assay turnaround from 3 - 4 weeks to 3 - 5 days (MSALABS processing times for Fire & PhotonAssay™). This will allow the Company to provide stakeholders with rapid results across the portfolio, minimising time between operational execution and market release.
·
Material differences were observed at the Teep project
, with results below:
o
Teep project, BTCRK08,
40.56 g/t Au
(3.66 g/t Au upgrade)
o
Teep project, BTCRK05,
31.40 g/t Au
(3.74 g/t Au upgrade)
o
Teep project, BTCRK09,
7.89 g/t Au
(1.37 g/t Au downgrade)
·
The Teep project is a high-grade gold-silver project along the Walker Lane trend within Esmeralda County, Nevada and has been prioritised for immediate follow-up work (See announcement dated 18 June 2026)
·
Engagement of US-based group
Dahrouge Geological Consulting
to assist with groundwork, project management and technical assessment of projects. This significantly increases the Company's exploration capacity, enabling
upscaling of ground operations
, streamlining project management, and improving the prioritisation of targets across its US portfolio.
·
Key next steps
across the Amonett-Frank project include:
1. Modern surface sampling across the full interpreted strike of mineralisation.
2. Geological mapping to investigate the scale, extent and economic potential of structurally controlled epithermal mineralisation.
3. Progressing permitting work to advance towards active drilling.
CEO Commentary
Hewie Rattray, CEO of the Company, stated:
"This is a standout result for the Company. The 143.1 g/t gold assay is the highest grade recorded across our US portfolio and alongside previously reported high-grade results from separate workings, strengthens our confidence in the broader potential of Amonett-Frank.
With the assays now verified and Dahrouge appointed to expand our US exploration capacity, we are moving quickly to understand the scale of the mineralised system and advance the next phase of work across the Project."
The Amonett-Frank Project
The Amonett-Frank project was identified and staked as part of the Company's wider portfolio expansion strategy. The Company's geological consultant, Schiehallion Consulting, conducted fieldwork as part of a due diligence programme over the project in May 2026. Surface samples from this due diligence work have now reported assay results up to 143.1 g/t Au, prompting immediate follow-up fieldwork and technical assessment.
The Project comprises 18 unpatented mineral claims over 371.88 acres (1.5km2) (Figure 1). The staked ground follows the approximate strike of structurally controlled high-grade gold-silver mineralisation within the project. The strike is marked by 2 shafts, 2 adits and 7 prospect pits from historical workings. The current blocks allow for 1.5 km of untested strike potential. Immediate follow-up will focus on the historical workings and extending the strike potential through geological mapping and surface programmes.
Figure 1: Amonett-Frank Project Plan, Pershing County, Nevada - New assays in RED

Assay Results
The Company has received the final assay results from the due diligence rock chip sampling programme completed across Amonett-Frank by the Company's geological consultant, Schiehallion Consulting, in May 2026 (Figure 1).
These additional samples were submitted alongside a Fire Assay QA/QC of PhotonAssay™ results. The new samples returned high-grade gold mineralisation, including
143.1 g/t Au
,

(Table 2). These samples complete the due diligence programme for the Project; next steps will focus on understanding the scale, extent, and controls of mineralisation at the Project.

The result of
143.1 g/t Au
(4.60 oz/t Au) represents the highest gold grade returned to date across the Company's US gold portfolio and is consistent with the high-grade, structurally controlled mineralisation identified previously within the Project.
Together with the original due diligence sampling reporting results up to 52.66 g/t Au and 15.73 g/t Au, these results provide confidence in the consistency of previously identified high-grade mineralisation at the Project. This also provides the Company with high-grade gold results from multiple historical workings within Amonett-Frank, supporting the interpretation of a mineralised corridor extending along the identified trend. The next stage of exploration will focus on the full 1.5 km strike length of this vein network and on understanding the economic potential of Amonett-Frank.
Fire Assay Verification and QA/QC
Samples collected during the Company's due diligence programme were dried, crushed and pulverised by MSALABS and analysed using Chrysos Corporation's PhotonAssay™ method with a sample detection limit of 0.015 ppm.
As part of the Company's standard QA/QC protocol, all PhotonAssay™ results across the Company's US projects were re-submitted for conventional fire assay with AAS or gravimetric finish to verify the reported grades. While PhotonAssay™ is a new technique, it is a certified and compliant analytical method. The fire assay technique has a long history of providing accurate and reliable results and was run for internal confirmation of sample integrity.
Due to operational timing, the final Amonett-Frank samples were submitted with the fire assay batch. Delays were incurred as the Amonett-Frank samples were overlimit (>100 g/t Au), requiring two gravimetric runs for QA/QC; the final gravimetric QA/QC result reported 143.1 g/t Au for BTCRK33.
The fire assay results returned grades comparable to the corresponding PhotonAssay™ results; some material differences were observed at Teep (>10% change from PhotonAssay™ to Fire Assay) (Table 3), but overall, the PhotonAssay™ was found to be accurate and consistent. This provides a high degree of confidence in the analytical results previously reported to the market across its US portfolio. Regarding the difference, the sample descriptors include 'metallic fragments' (Table 2), and material differences across the two techniques suggest that coarse gold has affected the grade and variability observed in the results of Teep and Amonett-Frank.
This also provides confidence in the PhotonAssay™ technique, which will reduce assay turnaround from 3 - 4 weeks (Approximate Fire Assay turnaround) to 3-5 days (Approximate PhotonAssay™ turnaround). Utilising this new technique will allow the Company to provide stakeholders with rapid results and updates across the portfolio, minimising the time between operational execution and market release.

Project Location
Figure 2: Amonett-Frank and Huntington-Whitman Project location, Nevada
The Amonett-Frank Project is in the Goldbanks Mining District of Pershing County, Nevada (Figure 2), the largest gold-producing state in the United States. Located approximately 31 miles (50km) south of Winnemucca within the Great Basin region, the project lies within a rapidly emerging gold province characterised by comparable mineral systems (epithermal-hot-springs Au/Ag) (Coolbaugh, 2011). The Project is proximal to Kinross U.S.'s Goldbanks project (Kinross U.S., NYSE: KGC), SSR Mining's long-running Marigold open-pit heap-leach mine and Nevada Gold Mines' Phoenix operation. The Project complements the Company's Huntington-Whitman Project to the north and extends the Company's Nevada footprint into a second productive district.
Goldbanks Au Project,
a significant epithermal deposit in the immediate area, holds an endowment of 2.56 Moz Au and 7.47 Moz Ag with current Proven and Probable Mineral Reserves consisting of a total of 166 Mt @ 0.48 g/t Au (Stone, 2010), Kinross U.S., NYSE: KGC.
Marigold Gold Mine
, continuous production since 1989, Marigold is a large run-of-mine heap leach operation. Probable Mineral Reserves consist of 2.98 Moz Au, with 174.8 Mt @ 0.47 g/t Au; an additional 0.346 Moz Au exists in leach pad inventory (SSR Mining, 2024). SSR also maintain active exploration in the region. SSR Mining, NASDAQ: SSRM.
Phoenix Gold Mine
, one of six mines included in the major Nevada Gold Mines (NGM) Barrick / Newmont joint venture. Proven and Probable Mineral Reserves consist of 2 Moz Au with 110 Mt @ 0.58 g/t Au, and 0.23 Mt Cu with 130 Mt @ 0.18% Cu (Barrick, 2025).
Project Geology
Amonett-Frank covers a strike of historical high-grade gold-silver workings developed on a set of epithermal hot-spring Au/Ag quartz veins and breccias. Each vein is up to 4 feet (1.2 m) wide and has been traced over several hundred metres (Johnson, 1977). The country rock is the Late Permian Golconda Terrane, comprising carbonates, basinal sediments, volcanics, and terrigenous clastic rocks. The USGS historically classified the occurrence as a hot-spring Au-Ag system (USGS deposit model 25a), an interpretation supported by recent due diligence observations by a qualified geologist. The Company considers this mineral system a compelling exploration target, as it is associated with significant precious-metal deposits across the Great Basin (Coolbaugh, 2011).
The deposit was discovered in 1933, with the first recorded production in 1935, when an unknown volume of gold ore was shipped from the property (Vanderburg, 1936). Documented workings comprise two shafts to approximately 80 feet (24 m) depth, short tunnels (adits) and lateral workings developed across the epithermal veins.
The Company's field review identified the structural trend described in the literature and confirmed the locations of historically recorded shafts, adits, and prospect pits, all of which are consistent with the historically reported mining activity (Vanderburg, 1936). The absence of any on-site processing facility, combined with historical accounts of ore being trucked from the property, is interpreted to suggest selective sampling of gold ore that would meet the economic standards of the 1930s.
This selective sampling, high historical cut-off grade, and very limited shallow exploration have left significant exploration gaps. Early results provide evidence of high-grade mineralisation at surface across several historical workings; further workings have yet to be sampled, and the full strike of mineralisation is not yet understood. Investigating the full extent of the mineralised corridor at Amonett-Frank positions the Company to deliver early drill-ready targets and to define this potentially economic system.
Figure 3: Amonett-Frank Project, location of central prospect marked by a ferric-manganiferous quartz breccia zone, several quartz networks and two historical mine shafts
Appointment of US Technical Consultant
The Company has engaged Dahrouge Geological Consulting to work alongside Schiehallion Consulting on technical assessment, field operations and project management across its US portfolio. Dahrouge is an established North American geological consultancy with its US office in Denver, Colorado, relevant for the Company's operations in Nevada and Arizona. Schiehallion Consulting continues as the Company's technical adviser working alongside Dahrouge.
The engagement is intended to significantly increase the Company's exploration capacity and provide in-country operational capability and direct experience of US permitting processes. It is intended to enable the Company to establish additional field crews and run multiple field programmes across its existing projects, while continuing to stake new ground and develop its project pipeline. This will also support an effective and efficient exploration process without operational strain.
Dahrouge will also assist with technical assessments of the Company's existing projects and advisory support on the federal and state permitting required to advance each project towards drill testing.
Forward Work Programme
Follow-up work at the Amonett-Frank project will include:
• Comprehensive rock-chip sampling of all identified historical workings within the Amonett-Frank Project.
• Geological mapping and further surface sampling to investigate the possible extension of structurally controlled epithermal mineralisation.
• Compilation of geoscientific data to assist in the understanding of the local geology and structural setting to provide drill-ready targets.
Follow-up work at the US portfolio scale will include:
• Working with Dahrouge to develop the technical understanding of existing projects and define next steps, with a focus on preparing targets for imminent fieldwork.
• Mobilisation of field teams on existing gold projects to commence their respective work programmes.
• Progression of further gold project staking in Nevada and Arizona, in line with the Company's previously announced phased strategy.
Figure 4: London BTC Company gold-silver project portfolio, State of Nevada
Further Staking and Portfolio Expansion
Schiehallion Consulting continues to actively advance the identification, evaluation and staking of additional prospective gold projects across Nevada and Arizona, with the intention of building a portfolio of high-quality, complementary assets.
The Company will provide further updates as additional projects are secured.
Cautionary Statement
This announcement contains references to historical production sourced from third-party reports, public databases, technical literature and government reports. These historical results have not been verified by the Company, are not reported in compliance with any current Mineral Resource or Ore Reserve code and should not be relied upon as indicative of the prospectivity of the Project or any future resource, reserve or production from the Project.
All of the samples discussed in this release are selective in nature with a high potential for bias and should not be considered as being representative of the overall mineralised structure or zone.
PhotonAssay™ and fire assay are different analytical techniques and results obtained by the two methods are not directly equivalent. Comparisons between the two methods presented in this announcement are provided for verification purposes only.
Competent Persons Statement
The information in this report that relates to exploration results and technical information is based on information compiled by Fionnlagh (Finn) Hunter, Principal Geological Consultant, who is a Member of the Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy (AusIMM) and has sufficient experience of relevance to the styles of mineralisation and the types of deposits under consideration, and to the activities undertaken, to qualify as a Competent Person as defined in the 2012 Edition of the Joint Ore Reserves Committee (JORC) Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves. Mr Hunter consents to the inclusion in this report of the matters based on the information in the form and context in which it appears.
Issue of Shares
In addition, the Company announces that, as set out in the Company's
prospectus dated 24 December 2024 ("Prospectus"),
it had established the Vinanz Limited Employee Benefit Trust ("EBT"). The Company intends to
allot
and issue

new

(representing
16.67%
of the enlarged issued share capital of the Company). These ordinary shares shall be held in the EBT on trust pending transfer
to beneficiaries
upon the vesting (or exercise, as the case may be) of awards granted, and for such other purposes relating to the ongoing recruitment, retention and incentivisation of employees as may be recommended by the Company from time to time (subject to the approval of the Remuneration Committee and the trustees of the EBT). Further to disclosures in the Company's Prospectus, the beneficiaries of any future distribution of EBT Shares to employees and directors will be notified upon
award.
Application will be made to the London Stock Exchange ("LSE") for admission of the EBT Shares to trading on the
Main Market

pari passu

Following Admission, the total number of Ordinary Shares in the capital of the Company will be
436,756,839 with voting rights. This figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company's issued share capital pursuant to the Company's Articles.
